evals.prompt: In Jetpack Compose, does it matter whether I write Modifier.padding(16.dp).background(Color.Red) versus Modifier.background(Color.Red).padding(16.dp)? Explain what actually differs visually between the two.
evals.expected_output: Explains that modifiers apply as an ordered chain, so padding-then-background draws the background inside the padded area (background fills the smaller inset box), while background-then-padding draws the background first over the full size and then insets content, producing a visibly different colored area.

assertions.text: States that modifier order matters / is a chain
Describes the visual difference between the two orderings

evals.prompt: I have a Composable that takes a plain (non-annotated) Kotlin data class as a parameter, and it recomposes every time its parent recomposes even though the data class's values haven't changed. What's the likely cause and fix?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Compose can't prove the data class is stable without an @Immutable or @Stable annotation, so it can't safely skip recomposition, and recommends annotating the class.

Flags the missing key parameter on items() and explains that without a stable key, per-item remembered state (like animation or focus) can get attached to the wrong row when the list is reordered or mutated.

assertions.text: Explains a concrete consequence of missing keys, not just 'add a key'
